## How to use this guide

This lecture is **presentation-led** because no Meyer chapter was included in the Lecture 11 folder. The guide therefore follows the lecture deck closely and uses general pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic concepts only where they are explicitly invoked by the presentation.

**Lecture route:** Overview → PART 1: Circadian Rhythms → What Are Circadian Rhythms? → Core terminology → Core terminology continued… → Evolution of Circadian Clocks Circadian clocks are present → Evolution of Circadian Clocks Anticipation of daily → Suprachiasmatic Nucleus (SCN) → Food Anticipatory Activity (FAA) → Clock Genes Transcription-Translation Feedback Loop (TTFL) → Peripheral Clocks → PART 2: How the clock changes drugs → …
</div>

## Lecture concepts

### 1. Overview

Circadian rhythms review. Clock → drugs.

**What to know:**
- Circadian rhythms review
- Clock → drugs
- Drugs → clock

### 2. PART 1: Circadian Rhythms

PART 1: Circadian Rhythms Review.

**What to know:**
- PART 1: Circadian Rhythms Review

### 3. What Are Circadian Rhythms?

Sleep/wake cycles. Physiological processes.

**What to know:**
- Sleep/wake cycles
- Physiological processes
- Internally generated ○ ~24 hours

### 4. Core terminology

Actogram ○ Visualize circadian activity. Diurnal vs. nocturnal.

**What to know:**
- Actogram ○ Visualize circadian activity
- Diurnal vs. nocturnal
- Criteria of circadian rhythms: ○ Persists in constant conditions ○ Entrainable by external cues Mistlberger PSYC388 lecture slides

### 5. Core terminology continued…

Zeitgeber ○ German for “time giver”. Entrainment.

**What to know:**
- Zeitgeber ○ German for “time giver”
- Entrainment
- Advance vs. Delay
- Phase response curve ○ Light in early subjective night = delay ○ Light in late subjective night = advance ○ Light in mid subjective day = no effect

### 6. Evolution of Circadian Clocks Circadian clocks are present

Bacteria. Plants.

**What to know:**
- Bacteria
- Plants
- Animals

### 7. Evolution of Circadian Clocks Anticipation of daily

Light/dark. Social coordination.

**What to know:**
- Light/dark
- Social coordination
- Avoidance
- Foraging

### 8. Suprachiasmatic Nucleus (SCN)

Master clock. ~20 000 neurons.

**What to know:**
- Master clock
- ~20 000 neurons
- Entrains to LD cycle
- Host SCN sets phase DONOR HOST

### 9. Food Anticipatory Activity (FAA)

1-3 hrs before mealtime. Persists without SCN ○ or in clock gene KO Mistlberger PSYC388 lecture slides Michalik et al. (2025).

**What to know:**
- 1-3 hrs before mealtime
- Persists without SCN ○ or in clock gene KO Mistlberger PSYC388 lecture slides Michalik et al. (2025)

### 10. Clock Genes Transcription-Translation Feedback Loop (TTFL)

Cell autonomous. CLOCK + BMAL1.

**What to know:**
- Cell autonomous
- CLOCK + BMAL1
- PER + CRY ○ accumulate ○ repress ○ degrade ○ cycle restarts
- ~24 hours per loop

### 11. Peripheral Clocks

Nearly every tissue has a clock. SCN synchronizes ○ not generate.

**What to know:**
- Nearly every tissue has a clock
- SCN synchronizes ○ not generate
- No SCN → clocks persist ○ Drift apart
- 43% of protein-coding genes are rhythmic
- Liver had most rhythmic genes Takahashi lab (UT Southwestern, 2015)

### 12. PART 2: How the clock changes drugs

PART 2: How the clock changes drugs.

**What to know:**
- PART 2: How the clock changes drugs

### 13. Pharmacokinetics vs. Pharmacodynamics

PK ○ Absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion. PD ○ Receptors, signalling, response.

**What to know:**
- PK ○ Absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion
- PD ○ Receptors, signalling, response
- Rhythmic components

### 14. Absorption and distribution

Gastric emptying. Gut blood flow.

**What to know:**
- Gastric emptying
- Gut blood flow
- Lipid absorption
- Lipophilic drugs absorbed faster in daytime
- Blood-brain barrier efflux is clock-controlled in Drosophila Fujimuira & Ushijima (2023) Axelrod et al. (2023) Zhang et al. (2014)

### 15. Metabolism and excretion

Liver cytochrome P450 enzymes rhythmic. Kidney filtration rhythmic.

**What to know:**
- Liver cytochrome P450 enzymes rhythmic
- Kidney filtration rhythmic
- Acetometophen in mice ○ Toxicity is higher at night. ○ Rhythm lost in liver clock knockouts
- Barbituates ○ Time asleep varies across the day Matsunaga et al., (2004) DeBruyne et al. (2014)

### 16. Pharmacodynamics

Drug targets are often rhythmic. 56 of 100 top-selling drugs.

**What to know:**
- Drug targets are often rhythmic
- 56 of 100 top-selling drugs
- 119 of 250 WHO essential medicines
- Short half-life drugs most affected Zhang et al, (2014)

### 17. Chronotherapy in clinical practice

Cholesterol: evening statins. Asthma: nocturnal symptoms.

**What to know:**
- Cholesterol: evening statins
- Asthma: nocturnal symptoms
- Rheumatoid arthritis: morning stiffness
- IL-6 peaks @ night
- Blood pressure: no difference

### 18. PART 3: How drugs change the clock

PART 3: How drugs change the clock.

**What to know:**
- PART 3: How drugs change the clock

### 19. Photic input to the SCN

Pathway ○ ipRGCs → RHT → SCN ○ Not rods & coness. Transmitter: glutamate.

**What to know:**
- Pathway ○ ipRGCs → RHT → SCN ○ Not rods & coness
- Transmitter: glutamate
- NMDA antagonists block light shifts
- NMDA agonists shift Moshirpor et al., (2025)

### 20. Alcohol

Blocks light-induced advances. Dose dependent Ruby & Prosser (2009) Ruby & Prosser (2009).

**What to know:**
- Blocks light-induced advances
- Dose dependent Ruby & Prosser (2009) Ruby & Prosser (2009)

### 21. Non-photic arousal

A drug’s apparent effect on the clock may run through behaviour Van Reeth & Turek (1989).

**What to know:**
- A drug’s apparent effect on the clock may run through behaviour Van Reeth & Turek (1989)

### 22. Non-SCN clocks in the brain

FAA survives SCN lesion → FEO. Daily methamphetamine survives SCN lesion ○ MASCO.

**What to know:**
- FAA survives SCN lesion → FEO
- Daily methamphetamine survives SCN lesion ○ MASCO
- MASCO persists without canonical clock genes Honma & Honma (1995) Honma et al. (1986) Tataroglu et al. (2006)

### 23. Stimulants

Cocaine sensitization needs clock genes. Per1 gene is needed for CPP Abarca et al. (2002) Andretic et al. (1999).

**What to know:**
- Cocaine sensitization needs clock genes
- Per1 gene is needed for CPP Abarca et al. (2002) Andretic et al. (1999)

### 24. Caffeine

Caffeine delays the clock ~40 min ○ Half the effect of bright light Ruby et al. (2018).

**What to know:**
- Caffeine delays the clock ~40 min ○ Half the effect of bright light Ruby et al. (2018)

### 25. Melatonin

Melatonin: a chronobiotic ○ Timing > dose ○ Shifts SCN. Dexamethasone ○ Shifts liver but not SCN Burgess et al. (2022) Wang et al. (2018).

**What to know:**
- Melatonin: a chronobiotic ○ Timing > dose ○ Shifts SCN
- Dexamethasone ○ Shifts liver but not SCN Burgess et al. (2022) Wang et al. (2018)

### 26. Takeaways

Clocks are cell autonomous and hierarchical ○ SCN → peripheral tissues. The clock affects drugs through rhythmic PK and PD ○ time-of-day effects.

**What to know:**
- Clocks are cell autonomous and hierarchical ○ SCN → peripheral tissues
- The clock affects drugs through rhythmic PK and PD ○ time-of-day effects.
- Drugs affect the clock via ○ Photic & non photic If you take the same pill at 8am vs 8pm, is it the same drug?
